title: On‑Prem Cluster Init Roadmap & Checklist
content:
Purpose:
This doc is a pragmatic, runbook‑style roadmap for provisioning greenfield on‑prem Kubernetes clusters that need to support both bare metal (PXE/BMC) sites and vSphere‑hosted racks. It collects our current operational patterns, a proposed Terraform module layout, a staged cluster bootstrap sequence, and an upgrade/rollback playbook.

Scope and audience:
- Audience: SREs and infra engineers in private deployments and solutions engineering who will run or hand off on‑prem installs.
- Scope: initial hardware provisioning, network and DNS wiring notes, terraform module boundaries, kubeadm/cluster API choices, bootstrap sequence, canary upgrades and rollback. Not a full hardware ordering guide.

Assumptions:
- Customer provides BMC/IPMI access for bare metal racks OR vSphere credentials for virtualized racks.
- VLANs for management and tenant data are pre‑approved by netops; we do not design L2 here.
- Centralized KMS/HSM integration will be handled separately; we assume KMS API tokens are available.
- Persistent storage: customers will either expose a CSI‑compatible SAN (iSCSI/NFS/Ceph) or we deploy local‑PV/rook where allowed.

Goals:
- Single, repeatable Terraform-driven workflow that supports both provisioning models with a small set of well‑documented variables.
- Minimal manual steps during initial bootstrap with explicit escape hatches for air‑gapped or low‑bandwidth environments.
- Safe upgrade path with canary control plane and automated node draining.

High level workflow (greenfield):
1) Preflight and validation (remote): confirm BMC or vSphere creds, IP plan, DNS entries, NTP servers.
2) Provision infrastructure (terraform): networks, DNS records, DHCP scopes (bare metal), vSphere VMs (if using vSphere), and bootstrap services (Tinkerbell or MAAS HTTP/TF templates).
3) PXE/ignition distribution: ensure discovery image, ignition cloud‑config, SSH key injection, and kubeadm config are reachable.
4) First control plane node(s) -> etcd init -> cluster CA generation (kept in KMS or sealed secret).
5) Join additional control plane nodes and validate etcd quorum.
6) Worker pools created via Terraform or Cluster API and validated (node labels, taints, kubelet version).
7) Install CNI (calico/weave) and CSI, deploy core addons and monitoring (prometheus stack, node exporter).
8) Bake image (golden vm or PXE image) for worker homogeneous fleets.
9) Run functional smoke tests and performance validation (latency, DNS, kube-dns, storage IO).
10) Mark as ready and handoff runbook to oncall/ops.

Terraform module design notes (proposed):
- modules/networking: create VLANs, route tables, DHCP scopes (for bare metal), and DNS records. Inputs: vlan_ids, dhcp_ranges, dns_zone. Outputs: mgmt_subnet_id, dhcp_server_id.
- modules/baremetal-boot: interfaces with Tinkerbell/MAAS or IPXE templates. Handles discovery templates, ignition/cpio artifacts, and BMC credential store. Inputs: discovery_image_url, bmc_credentials_secret_ref. Outputs: boot_job_ids.
- modules/vsphere-vm: thin wrapper for creating control plane and worker VMs (supports cloudInit and guest customization). Inputs: template, cpu, mem, disk, network. Outputs: vm_ids, guest_ips.
- modules/k8s-control-plane: creates kubeadm config secret, kubelet config, and bootstraps the first control plane using local exec or remote-exec with SSH. Inputs: kube_version, pod_cidr, service_cidr, ca_backend. Outputs: control_plane_endpoints, kubeconfig_secret_name.
- modules/node-pool: declarative node pools with lifecycle policies, autoscale hints and desired image version. Inputs: pool_size, image_ref, taints, labels. Outputs: node_names.
- modules/storage: glue for provisioning CSI storage classes, PVs, and optional Rook/Ceph bootstrap. Inputs: storage_backend_type, storage_params. Outputs: default_storage_class.

Notes on module design: keep state per‑customer in a dedicated backend (s3/consul/terraform cloud). Use semantic module versions and tag releases in the terraform modules repo. Avoid encoding secrets directly; reference secret manager paths (Vault/KMS).

Bootstrap sequence details (example commands / snippets):
- Prechecks:
  - ping DNS and NTP: "curl -sfS --max-time 5 https://metadata.local || true"
  - verify BMC: "ipmitool -I lanplus -H $BMC -U admin -P *** chassis power status"
- Run provisioning (bare metal example):
  # create DHCP/DNS/boot artifacts
  terraform init && terraform apply -target=module.networking -var-file=site.tfvars
  terraform apply -target=module.baremetal-boot -var-file=site.tfvars
- Control plane (handed off from terraform as an ssh action):
  ssh ubuntu@control-0 'sudo kubeadm init --config /etc/kubeadm/config.yaml --upload-certs'
  scp ~/.kube/config ops@jumpbox:/tmp/cluster-kubeconfig
- Join worker nodes:
  ssh worker-1 'sudo kubeadm join --token <token> <control-endpoint> --discovery-token-ca-cert-hash sha256:<hash>'

Operational runbook snippets:
- If a control plane node fails during bootstrap:
  1) Inspect journalctl -u kubelet and kubeadm logs in /var/log/
  2) If etcd did not form, remove the failed member from the cluster and re-run kubeadm on a fresh host.
  3) If we lost more than 1/3 of etcd members, contact SRE lead and escalate to restore etcd snapshot from backups.

Upgrade plan (minor + patch upgrades):
- Strategy: control-plane first canary -> remaining control-plane -> worker pools by node-pool batch.
- Canary window: pick a single control-plane where we apply kubeadm upgrade and kubelet bump; validate API server, telemetry, and read latency for 30m.
- Worker rolling update: cordon -> drain with --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data -> upgrade kubelet and kube-proxy -> uncordon. Batch size: default 20% or configured per pool.
- Persistent volumes: ensure CSI sidecars are updated in advance and that in‑flight IO is validated. For CSI migrations, follow upstream migration guide and schedule a storage freeze window.

Rollback plan and safety nets:
- Control plane: keep an etcd snapshot before any control plane upgrade (automate snapshot via etcdctl to an offsite S3 bucket). If upgrade fails, restore etcd snapshot to previous revision and re‑deploy previous kube‑apiserver image.
- Workers: if a worker fails to join after node image/kubelet bump, reprovision using previous gold image or restart kubelet with previous binary.
- Terraform state: use feature branch with an explicit apply approval. If terraform changes introduce drift, use terraform state replace or rollback to tagged state backup.

Preflight checklist (must pass before scheduled bootstrap):
- BMC or vSphere creds validated and saved in Vault.
- DHCP range reserved and documented.
- DNS A records for control plane endpoints created (or expected dynamic A records supported).
- NTP reachable from destination network with <=100ms jitter.
- KMS token available for certificate sealing.
- Storage backend reachable (sufficient capacity).
- Runbook owners informed and on‑call scheduled for the window.

Risk matrix (brief):
- Risk: etcd quorum loss => Impact: high => Mitigation: preflight backup, 3+ control-plane nodes, test restore.
- Risk: broken CNI upgrade => Impact: high => Mitigation: dry run in staging, schedule maintenance.
- Risk: BMC unresponsive => Impact: medium => Mitigation: have IPMI out‑of‑band console access plan and manual provisioning fallback.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Decide: full Cluster API approach vs kubeadm + terraform + local exec for first pass (recommendation: start with kubeadm for simplicity, roadmap cluster-api for later automated lifecycle).
- Add a small terraform helper to rotate KMS tokens during bootstrap to avoid manual steps.
- Define golden image bake pipeline for both baremetal PXE and vSphere template creation.
- Audit and add explicit firewall rules needed for Prometheus/node exporter communication.

Appendix: quick commands and checks
- Verify pod network: kubectl get pods -n kube-system -o wide | grep calico
- Check nodes: kubectl get nodes -o wide
- Quick etcd snapshot: ETCDCTL_API=3 etcdctl snapshot save /tmp/etcd-$(date +%F).db --endpoints=https://127.0.0.1:2379 --cert=/etc/kubernetes/pki/etcd/peer.crt --key=/etc/kubernetes/pki/etcd/peer.key --cacert=/etc/kubernetes/pki/etcd/ca.crt
- Recreate a worker with terraform: terraform apply -target=module.node-pool.aws_instance.worker-pool[2] -var-file=site.tfvars

Notes to self (informal):
- Keep the first pass simple: kubeadm and terraform is lowest cognitive load for customers we support today.
- For airgapped installs, ship an ops USB with artifacts and a compact script to run the exact apply sequence.
- Make sure to capture common failure logs in the bootstrap terraform outputs to speed debugging.

Contact and handoff:
- Oncall rotation: eng-private-deployments on-call channel (#eng-private-deployments).
- Handoff checklist to customer success: kubeconfig + vault paths + backup locations + golden image IDs.

End of doc.
